key_insight: This paper argues that scientific ideas evolve like genomes: new ideas are built by inheriting mechanisms, fixing weaknesses, and recombining parts of earlier work. It introduces a benchmark to test whether AI can reason about this lineage and generate ideas grounded in it.
problem_solved: Current benchmarks do not adequately measure whether AI systems can trace how scientific ideas originate, evolve, and relate to prior work. This makes it hard to evaluate if models can generate novel research ideas that are still faithful to scientific lineage.
method: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a benchmark for scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation.
Organizes scientific papers or proposals using the IdeaGene framework, representing each as a set of minimal inherited components.
Evaluates whether AI systems can identify idea ancestry, reason about inherited mechanisms and limitations, and propose new ideas consistent with that lineage.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more realistic way to evaluate research-assistant models beyond simple retrieval or summarization. It can help build systems that generate novel ideas while staying scientifically grounded and traceable.
visual_elements: A genome-style lineage tree showing how one idea inherits and branches from prior papers.
A before/after diagram illustrating limitation -> repair -> new idea generation.
A benchmark pipeline graphic: paper set -> lineage reasoning -> grounded idea proposal -> evaluation.
Icons for inheritance, mutation/recombination, and scientific papers to reinforce the genome metaphor.
paper_title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
paper_authors: Yifan Zhou, Qihao Yang, Yan Li, Donggang Li, Xiru Hu
